title: Quantum Phases and Structural Transitions of Bosons in Bubble-Shaped Confinements
authors: Fabio Cinti, Gabriele Costa, Giuseppe Pellicane, Santi Prestipino, Matteo Ciardi
abstract: We investigate the structural properties and superfluid behavior of soft-core bosons confined in a spherical bubble trap at large particle numbers ($N \le 1800$). Using Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations with worm algorithm sampling in continuous space, we show that increasing $N$ drives a sequence of layering transitions: beyond the established bilayer supersolid, a third concentric layer of clusters emerges at $N \approx 1800$. By analyzing the distribution of permutation cycles distribution, we demonstrate that a finite superfluid fraction ($f_s \approx 10\%$) persists even in this multi-layer regime. These findings clarify the role of particle number in driving layer formation on curved manifolds, offering a concrete guide for future experiments with bubble-trapped bosons.
summary: This paper uses Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations to study soft-core bosons in a bubble-shaped trap. The research demonstrates that increasing the number of bosons drives the system through multiple structural layering transitions, forming a third concentric layer. Crucially, it shows that even in this complex, multi-layer state, a measurable superfluid fraction remains, providing key insights for experimental quantum gas physics.
main_problem: The study investigates the structural properties and superfluid behavior of soft-core bosons confined within a curved, bubble-shaped trap, focusing on how particle number drives structural transitions.
main_result: Increasing the particle number ($N$) induces a sequence of layering transitions, leading to the emergence of a third concentric cluster layer, while a finite superfluid fraction persists in this multi-layer regime.
method: The research employs Path Integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations using the worm algorithm in continuous space to calculate finite-temperature equilibrium properties.
model_or_system: The system consists of soft-core bosons interacting via a soft-core repulsive potential and confined by a bubble-shaped external potential $u_{	ext{ext}}(r)$. The study analyzes the system across varying particle numbers ($N$) and quantum fluctuation parameters ($\lambda$).
key_observables: Superfluid fraction ($f_s$), integrated radial density ($n(r)$), and the distribution of permutation cycles ($P(L)$).
important_parameters: Large particle numbers ($N \le 1800$), quantum fluctuation parameter ($\lambda$), and trap geometry parameters ($R, u_0, \Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the soft-core potential allows multiple bosons to occupy the same cluster, and the work extends previous findings to a large-$N$ regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the bubble-trap potential, compare trap potentials in different gravitational settings, show worldline snapshots demonstrating the transition from single-layer crystal to bilayer supersolid to uniform superfluid shell, and visualize the nucleation of a third outer shell as $N$ increases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical system and Hamiltonian, detailing the PIMC methodology, presenting results showing the evolution of phases (crystal $	o$ supersolid $	o$ superfluid) with quantum fluctuations ($\lambda$), and finally extending the analysis to large particle numbers ($N$) to observe multi-layer structure formation.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, quantitative guidance on how particle number dictates structural organization in curved quantum systems, which is highly relevant for experimental realization in trapped atomic gases.
